axis: no skill called for or shown → incapacity worth condemning

members.tone: Classifying rather than condemning - it covers work that asks for no special skill just as evenly as a hand that has none, where *botchy* is already a verdict on the result.
Names an absence rather than a mess - what is made shows no art in it, which is a thinner charge than the spoilage *botched* points at.
Dismissive and slightly contemptuous - the badness is lumpy and visible, something you can see in the thing itself.
The most violent way to call work bad - it makes the poor doing sound like hacking, where *botchy* only makes it look untidy.
The flat, unloaded member of its set - it states that the doing fell short of skill and stops, supplying none of the disgust in *butcherly*.
Settles the failure as done and irreversible - the thing was spoiled in the handling and now stands spoiled.
Coarser than *bungled* - the spoiling is crude and shows, a wreck left behind rather than a slip.
Turns the ineptitude into a standing quality - not one attempt gone wrong but the manner of the doer.
The gentlest of its set and the most forgivable - it faults the handling while *incompetent* faults the capacity.
Catches the lack of skill in motion - hands groping and losing hold, rather than the finished judgement *incompetent* delivers.
The formal verdict of the family - it withholds the aptitude altogether, where *clumsy* grants it and blames only the execution.
Faults the making as unrefined and hastily finished, an aesthetic complaint rather than the flat incapacity of *incompetent*.
The mildest complaint available about workmanship - it concedes the care was not taken while leaving *crude* to sound the note of coarseness.
Aimed at the person and not the product, it writes off the ability rather than the attempt, with an exasperation that can shade into fondness.
